extraction.Name: Edward Janis, junior
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment at the time it was mailed to him, for he did not want to pay taxes, but he took it, as he was advised that it would be taxed any way
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged it to the State of South Dakota—called The Rule Credit Loan—for $500.00
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to the State of South Dakota (The Rule Credit Loan) for $500.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the taxes got behind up to 1920, when he mortgaged it to the State of South Dakota—called The Rule Credit Loan—for $500.00; that he paid off these taxes out of this loan, and used the balance for living expenses; that the taxes are now behind, and have been since 1920
extraction.Occupation/Income: he farms for a living, and this is the only source of his income
extraction.NOTES: Has a wife and seven children, all of whom have good health; hailed out quite frequently in his territory; has kept up his payments on the loan; no other debts against this allotment; has never received any help from the County or Government; affidavit sworn November 21, 1928
